purpose: A finite retrospective baseline for strategy expression, compiler fidelity, composition and authoring cost; not universal expressiveness or hardware accuracy.
freeze_policy: Requirements and denominators are fixed before writing this campaign's adapters. Known implementation gaps remain in the denominator. This is not a blind held-out study.
scope: Declared CPU plus one GPU, Dense and trace-driven MoE, finite layer/request traces, DRAM/VRAM, explicit synthetic prices. No hardware measurements or accuracy refits.

status_policy.unsupported: An unimplemented strategy is a coverage gap, not an invalid strategy and not a passing negative case.
status_policy.dead_end: Policy inability to advance is not proof of global infeasibility.
status_policy.oracle: Expected semantics must be handwritten before each execution; compiler output is only the observed side. Existing handwritten references may be reused transparently.

basic.name: Module placement
basic.requirement: Two layers use CPU for layer0 dense_ffn and GPU for layer1 dense_ffn without changing other task devices.
basic.oracle: Exact per-layer device bindings, charged cross-device input/output movement, dependencies preserved.

basic.name: Phase placement
basic.requirement: GPU prefill then CPU decode in a persistent two-layer trace.
basic.oracle: Phase devices, stable KV identities/bytes, charged GPU-to-CPU KV copies, history growth.

basic.name: Attention stages
basic.requirement: Refine Attention, place QK/softmax on CPU and PV/output on GPU.
basic.oracle: Handwritten operand identities and tensor bytes, Q/K and probability transfers, no missing dependencies.

basic.name: FFN tensor partition
basic.requirement: Partition intermediate dimension 16 into CPU [0,4) and GPU [4,16), then sum partial outputs.
basic.oracle: Gate/up/down leaf geometry totals 1536 bytes at H=8 F32; one 32-byte CPU partial return; exact SUM inputs.

basic.name: Layer and round ordering
basic.requirement: Run two Dense layers over prefill and multiple decode rounds without inventing module barriers or resetting persistent state.
basic.oracle: Every consumer waits for its producer, every intended invocation completes once, persistent KV versions and identities remain valid.

basic.name: Subbatch execution pipeline
basic.requirement: Declare at least two independently scheduled subbatches with CPU Attention and GPU FFN so one subbatch's CPU stage overlaps another's GPU stage.
basic.oracle: One high-level declaration names the stage/subbatch schedule; actual positive-duration cross-subbatch compute overlap and correct per-request dependencies. A list of serialized tasks or transform-pass pipeline alone is insufficient.

basic.name: Weight retention and reuse
basic.requirement: Keep reusable weights across invocations when the cache budget permits.
basic.oracle: Stable tensor identity, no redundant weight reload for retained copies, every reservation counted against one shared budget.

basic.name: Safe eviction under pressure
basic.requirement: Use a cache too small for both layer weights but large enough for one; evict safe weights to progress.
basic.oracle: Recorded EVICT of a non-running weight, no in-flight input eviction, peak cached weight payload including reservations within the budget, completed policy.

basic.name: Cross-layer prefetch
basic.requirement: Prepare next-layer weights using known layer order while current-layer execution is active.
basic.oracle: At least one charged cross-layer prefetch COPY starts before current-layer work completes; it is not merely a startup preload.

basic.name: Scoped CE/SM transport
basic.requirement: Layer0 weight copies use CE and layer1 use SM on one explicitly declared shared link.
basic.oracle: Actual COPY engine by static weight owner, service contract preserved, same cache budget and physical ledger.

basic.name: Causal MoE scheduling
basic.requirement: Schedule experts only after route revelation while allowing public static weight catalogues.
basic.oracle: Two private-future traces with identical public prefix produce identical prefix decisions; unrevealed expert execution is rejected.

basic.name: Resource-aware policy response
basic.requirement: A causal policy chooses or retains task placement using currently available CPU/memory state, without reading private future restoration.
basic.oracle: Different currently observed resource states cause the declared placement/release response; identical public prefixes with different private recovery cannot change earlier decisions. Fixed placement that merely waits is insufficient.

combinations.name: Attention stages + FFN partition
combinations.requirement: Both refinements coexist in one invocation, with both handwritten operand/byte contracts preserved.

combinations.name: FFN partition + startup preparation
combinations.requirement: Preload chosen GPU shard weights with charged copies before computation; shard merge stays correct.

combinations.name: Layer placement + cross-layer prefetch
combinations.requirement: Layer0 CPU FFN and layer1 GPU FFN coexist with actual charged next-layer prefetch.

combinations.name: Phase placement + persistent KV migration
combinations.requirement: Phase devices change while KV identity/history and charged migration remain correct.

combinations.name: Scoped transport + constrained shared cache
combinations.requirement: CE/SM owner-specific copies plus safe eviction respect a single undersized global cache budget.

combinations.name: MoE routing + expert cache + CPU/GPU placement
combinations.requirement: Revealed expert tasks use declared heterogeneous placement and bounded expert caching without route leakage.

combinations.name: Subbatch pipeline + cross-layer prefetch
combinations.requirement: B06's explicit cross-subbatch compute overlap coexists with charged next-layer prefetch and one resource ledger.

combinations.name: Local Attention refinement + phase placement
combinations.requirement: Refine only a selected request's Attention within an invocation and place prefill/decode tasks differently; unselected requests remain unchanged.

combinations.name: Different FFN partitions in disjoint regions
combinations.requirement: Apply two different FFN partitions to two disjoint requests inside one invocation; preserve shared physical weight ownership without duplicate uncharged copies.

combinations.name: Scoped transport + scoped preparation + phase placement
combinations.requirement: Layer-scoped preparation/CE-SM choices and phase-specific execution agree under one cache budget.

combinations.name: Attention + FFN partition + startup preparation
combinations.requirement: All three mechanisms coexist, preserve exact operands/bytes, and complete under shared capacity.

combinations.name: Memory response + prefetch + cache
combinations.requirement: Under an explicit memory reclaim event, prefetch/cache safely release or defer work and the causal controller acknowledges only after safe release, with decision cost charged.

negative.name: Overlapping FFN partitions
negative.requirement: Reject overlapping shard intervals as invalid before execution.

negative.name: Incomplete FFN coverage
negative.requirement: Reject a gap/incomplete intermediate-dimension partition as invalid.

negative.name: Missing or wrong FFN merge
negative.requirement: Reject missing/incorrect SUM arity rather than dropping a partial output.

negative.name: Producer dependency violation
negative.requirement: Reject COMPUTE before its required input is ready with the specific dependency/readiness error.

negative.name: In-flight input eviction
negative.requirement: Reject evicting an input copy from the domain of an active computation.

negative.name: Capacity overflow
negative.requirement: Reject a concrete oversized COPY with a capacity error, not Unsupported or a global infeasibility claim.

negative.name: Conflicting scoped choices
negative.requirement: Reject incomparable equal-priority conflicting rules instead of silently choosing declaration order.

negative.name: Unrevealed expert execution
negative.requirement: Reject targeting a private future expert task before route revelation for the information-boundary reason.

authoring.name: Change module placement
authoring.requirement: Change layer0 FFN from GPU to CPU by strategy declaration only; verify device and data movement.

authoring.name: Change FFN partition ratio
authoring.requirement: Change CPU/GPU split from 4/12 to 12/4 with explicit matching synthetic prices; verify geometry and merge.

authoring.name: Change cache budget
authoring.requirement: Change shared budget so a successful policy must safely evict weights; no compiler/modeling edits.

authoring.name: Enable cross-layer prefetch
authoring.requirement: Switch prefetch off/on using only strategy declarations and observe charged earlier next-layer copies.

authoring.name: Change transfer engine
authoring.requirement: Change one layer's weight engine CE to SM using the same explicit link contract and verify actual copies.

authoring.name: Change resource-response rule
authoring.requirement: Switch the declared causal resource-response rule under the same memory/CPU scenario and verify the expected response change.

authoring_measurement: Successful task count and unchanged compiler/modeling hashes are measured. Record authored nonblank/noncomment lines including task-specific helpers. Do not fabricate a hand-written low-level baseline, human completion time, readability result or compression percentage if no fair paired baseline exists.
